raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

`VocabParallelEmbedding.get_masked_input_and_mask` (`vocab_parallel_embedding.py`) and `apply_rotary_pos_emb_native` (`rotary_embedding/utils.py`) are both `@torch.compile`-decorated without an XPU guard. torch.compile/Inductor codegen on Intel XPU under tensor parallelism is unreliable for these functions, causing either:

- a scheduler watchdog timeout (stuck in Inductor's compile-worker subprocess, visible in a thread dump under `torch/_inductor/compile_worker/subproc_pool.py`), or
- a hard crash: `RuntimeError: level_zero backend failed with error: 20 (UR_RESULT_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST)` or `error: 40 (UR_RESULT_ERROR_OUT_OF_RESOURCES)`, surfacing at the next CPU/GPU sync point (e.g. a `.item()` call in an unrelated function further down the call stack), which makes the crash site misleading relative to the actual cause.

This affects any TP>1 model on `intel_xpu` that routes position-embedding lookups through `VocabParallelEmbedding`/`ParallelLMHead`, or that calls `apply_rotary_pos_emb` from `rotary_embedding/utils.py` (used directly by some vision towers and `gemma3_causal.py`, separate from the `RotaryEmbedding` class in `rotary_embedding/base.py`, which already has proper XPU handling via a dedicated fused kernel).

`sglang/srt/speculative/spec_utils.py` already guards an identical `torch.compile` pattern with `disable=_is_npu or _is_xpu` — these two call sites were simply missed when XPU support was added elsewhere in the codebase.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/srt/layers/vocab_parallel_embedding.py`: add `_is_xpu = is_xpu()`, change `get_masked_input_and_mask`'s decorator from `disable=_is_npu` to `disable=_is_npu or _is_xpu`.
- `python/sglang/srt/layers/rotary_embedding/utils.py`: add `_is_xpu = is_xpu()`, change `apply_rotary_pos_emb_native`'s decorator from no `disable` argument to `disable=_is_xpu`. (Left NPU behavior here untouched — this decorator previously compiled unconditionally, including on `apply_rotary_pos_emb_npu`'s fallback path for shapes it doesn't support, and I haven't validated disabling compile there, so I didn't bundle an NPU behavior change into an XPU fix.)

## Accuracy Tests

Validated on real hardware (4x Intel Arc Pro B60, TP4, `intel_xpu` backend) running a vision-language model whose vision tower hits both call sites (position-embedding lookup via `VocabParallelEmbedding`, and rotary embeddings via `apply_rotary_pos_emb` in the vision attention path):

- Before fix: crashed on the very first vision-embedding lookup (0% progress), every run.
- After the `vocab_parallel_embedding.py` fix alone: progressed much further, but a full-dataset accuracy run still crashed partway through (~20%) with the same `UR_RESULT_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST` signature, now originating from the second, previously-unidentified `apply_rotary_pos_emb_native` compile site.
- After both fixes together (plus a request-concurrency cap to stay within available device memory, unrelated to this change): a full accuracy run completed end to end with zero crashes across multiple runs (300 and 5349 examples), accuracy scores in the expected range for the task and model.

Also added `test/registered/xpu/test_vocab_rotary_torch_compile_xpu_guard.py`, run on the same hardware:
- Direct regression check that `torch.compile` is actually disabled on XPU for both functions (checks for the absence of `_torchdynamo_orig_callable` -- `torch.compile(fn, disable=True)` returns `fn` itself, unwrapped). Verified these two assertions fail if the `_is_xpu` guard is reverted, so they'd catch a future regression without needing to reproduce the original multi-GPU TP hang/crash.
- Functional correctness of both functions on an XPU device, parametrized over dtypes/shapes.
- All 12 tests pass with the fix in place.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable — this change only disables `torch.compile` for the XPU device path (no effect on CUDA/CPU/NPU), replacing an unreliable/crashing compiled kernel with the existing eager fallback. No speed comparison was run since the XPU path did not previously complete.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

@@ -0,0 +1,116 @@
+"""Regression test for the XPU torch.compile guard on
+``VocabParallelEmbedding.get_masked_input_and_mask`` and
+``apply_rotary_pos_emb_native``.
+
+Both functions are ``@torch.compile``-decorated. torch.compile/Inductor
+codegen on Intel XPU under tensor parallelism is unreliable for them,
+previously causing either a scheduler watchdog timeout (stuck in Inductor's
+compile-worker subprocess) or a hard crash ("RuntimeError: level_zero backend
+failed with error: 20/40") on real multi-GPU TP servers. That failure mode
+needs a full TP server under sustained load to reproduce, so it isn't
+practical to reproduce directly in a unit test; instead this test locks in
+the fix itself (torch.compile is actually disabled on XPU, not just
+numerically correct) plus functional correctness on an XPU device.
+"""
+
+import sys
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.layers.rotary_embedding.utils import (
+    apply_rotary_pos_emb,
+    apply_rotary_pos_emb_native,
+    apply_rotary_pos_emb_native_eager,
+)
+from sglang.srt.layers.vocab_parallel_embedding import get_masked_input_and_mask
+from sglang.srt.utils import is_xpu
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_xpu_ci
+
+register_xpu_ci(est_time=10, suite="nightly-xpu-kernel-main-1-gpu", nightly=True)
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(not is_xpu(), reason="XPU required")
+
+DEVICE = "xpu"
+
+
+def _assert_not_dynamo_wrapped(fn) -> None:
+    # torch.compile(fn, disable=True) returns fn itself, unwrapped -- no
+    # _torchdynamo_orig_callable attribute gets attached. If a future edit
+    # drops the `or _is_xpu` guard, this function would instead be a dynamo
+    # wrapper and this assertion catches it immediately, without needing to
+    # reproduce the original multi-GPU TP compile-worker hang/crash.
+    assert not hasattr(fn, "_torchdynamo_orig_callable"), (
+        f"{fn.__name__} is torch.compile-wrapped on XPU -- the _is_xpu guard "
+        "appears to have been removed"
+    )
+
+
+def test_get_masked_input_and_mask_not_compiled_on_xpu():
+    _assert_not_dynamo_wrapped(get_masked_input_and_mask)
+
+
+def test_apply_rotary_pos_emb_native_not_compiled_on_xpu():
+    _assert_not_dynamo_wrapped(apply_rotary_pos_emb_native)
+    # The platform dispatcher (used directly by e.g. the vision attention
+    # path) must resolve to this same guarded function on XPU.
+    assert apply_rotary_pos_emb is apply_rotary_pos_emb_native
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("dtype", [torch.bfloat16, torch.float16, torch.float32])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("input_dtype", [torch.int32, torch.int64])
+def test_get_masked_input_and_mask_correctness_xpu(dtype, input_dtype):
+    cfg = dict(
+        org_vocab_start_index=16,
+        org_vocab_end_index=32,
+        num_org_vocab_padding=0,
+        added_vocab_start_index=64,
+        added_vocab_end_index=64,
+    )
+    # Include negative and garbage ids: the mask is the only defense against
+    # them when the OOB probe is disabled, so they must produce zero rows.
+    token_ids = [-100, -1, 0, 16, 17, 31, 32, 63, 2**30]
+    if input_dtype == torch.int64:
+        token_ids += [torch.iinfo(torch.int64).min, torch.iinfo(torch.int64).max]
+    input_ids = torch.tensor(token_ids, dtype=input_dtype, device=DEVICE)
+
+    masked_input, input_mask = get_masked_input_and_mask(input_ids, **cfg)
+
+    weight = torch.randn((16, 8), dtype=dtype, device=DEVICE)
+    output = torch.nn.functional.embedding(masked_input.long(), weight)
+    output.masked_fill_(input_mask.unsqueeze(-1), 0)
+
+    expected_mask = torch.tensor(
+        [True, True, True, False, False, False, True, True, True]
+        + ([True, True] if input_dtype == torch.int64 else []),
+        device=DEVICE,
+    )
+    torch.testing.assert_close(input_mask, expected_mask)
+    # In-vocab rows (org or added) embed normally; everything else is zeroed.
+    assert torch.all(output[input_mask] == 0)
+    assert not torch.any(torch.all(output[~input_mask] == 0, dim=-1))
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("num_tokens", [1, 257])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("head_size", [64, 128])
+def test_apply_rotary_pos_emb_correctness_xpu(num_tokens: int, head_size: int):
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    num_heads, num_kv_heads = 8, 1
+    q = torch.randn(num_tokens, num_heads, head_size, device=DEVICE)
+    k = torch.randn(num_tokens, num_kv_heads, head_size, device=DEVICE)
+    cos = torch.randn(num_tokens, head_size, device=DEVICE)
+    sin = torch.randn(num_tokens, head_size, device=DEVICE)
+
+    q_expected, k_expected = apply_rotary_pos_emb_native_eager(
+        q.clone(), k.clone(), cos, sin
+    )
+    # On XPU this is the exact same (uncompiled) code path as the eager
+    # reference above -- bit-for-bit parity is expected, not just "close".
+    q_actual, k_actual = apply_rotary_pos_emb(q.clone(), k.clone(), cos, sin)
+
+    torch.testing.assert_close(q_actual, q_expected, rtol=0, atol=0)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(k_actual, k_expected, rtol=0, atol=0)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(pytest.main([__file__, "-v", "-s"]))
